::api-operation{method="POST" path="/v1/email_webhooks/ses"}
#docs
UNAUTHENTICATED by design — AWS SNS cannot present an API key, so authenticity comes from the SNS signature instead, verified before anything is read. SNS posts `text/plain`, and the raw bytes are kept because the signature is computed over them. A `SubscriptionConfirmation` is confirmed automatically, but only AFTER the signature verifies, since the callback URL is attacker-supplied otherwise. Always answers 200 for a verified message — including one it ignores — because a non-2xx makes SNS retry a notification that was understood.

## Headers

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | `string` | no | Safely retry writes — repeats return the original response. If a write FAILED after it had already taken effect, that failure is what repeats: the key is spent, and a new attempt needs a new key. |

## Response

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `received` | `boolean` | Always true; the event was received. One of `true`. |
| `confirmed` | `boolean` | Present on a SubscriptionConfirmation. |
| `ignored` | `boolean` | Present when the message carried no actionable feedback. |

## Status codes

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Verified and handled |
| `400` | Body is not JSON |
| `403` | SNS signature rejected |
| `409` | Idempotency-Key conflict — the key is already in flight, or was reused with a different request payload. |

#request
```bash [Request]
curl -X POST "$TMBILLING_URL/v1/email_webhooks/ses" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TMBILLING_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{}'
```

#response
:::code-group
```json [200 OK]
{
  "received": true,
  "confirmed": false,
  "ignored": false
}
```
```json [400 Bad Request]

    "message": "Body is not JSON"
  }
}
```

```json [403 Forbidden]
  }
}
```
```json [409 Conflict]

  "error": {
    "type": "idempotency_error",
```
